scenes.desc: La otra banda fundadora, preferida por los estadounidenses: para Pete Fornatale fijaron los estándares que todos los que vinieron detrás deben cumplir. Jimmy Page la formó al salir de los Yardbirds con el nombre de New Yardbirds; según la leyenda, Keith Moon profetizó que caerían «como un zepelín de plomo». Page y Robert Plant son el gran ejemplo del doble foco guitarra-voz del heavy, una rivalidad afectuosa en la que ninguno eclipsa al otro, y los aullidos de Plant son uno de los modelos del canto del género. Sus temas más dulces fueron siempre carne del formato de radio hard rock.

podcast.title: Apology and Compliment to The Trews
podcast.body: After his initial displeasure regarding The Trews' "Bohemian Rhapsody" cover, Robert Plant later offered a subtle apology during a show in Calgary at the Saddledome. He publicly acknowledged Canada's rich songwriting history, mentioning Neil Young, Joni Mitchell, and Leonard Cohen, and significantly, included "the trues" in this esteemed list. "Canada has always had such a rich history of songwriting and with Neil Young and Joni Mitchell and Leonard Cohen and the trues. And I took that as his his apology for telling us."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Disapproval of "Bohemian Rhapsody" Cover
podcast.body: Robert Plant expressed strong disapproval when The Trews performed a "punky version" of Queen's "Bohemian Rhapsody" during their shared tour, especially after it earned them a standing ovation. He conveyed his feelings by stating he knew Freddie Mercury and felt it was inappropriate to "relive the past," even directly accosting their drummer Sean about it. "He didn't want us doing that anymore... he told us it was because he knew Freddie and we're not here to relive the past."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Enduring Musical Figure
podcast.body: Robert Plant is a legendary singer who is regarded as a historical figure in music and has aged remarkably well. With 15, 16, or 17 albums under his belt, his new releases are always noteworthy. "Robert Plan es un mítico cantante que yo creo que ha envejecido muy bien, no es ahora mismo posiblemente lo más interesante para la estén musical pero es un, yo creo que hay un personaje histórico que sobre todo ya después de 15, 16 y a 17 discos de llevar de este hombre pues es un disco como no a tener en cuenta."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Fan of Big Black's Atomizer
podcast.body: Robert Plant, a renowned musician, declared himself a fan of Steve Albini after listening to Big Black's debut album, *Atomizer*. He was particularly impressed by the abrasive intensity and industrial sound of the record. "Robert Blant, que entre escucharlos se declararía Fanda Elbidi."

srcs.source: Central Sonora

podcast.title: Fats Domino Tribute
podcast.body: Robert Plant was one of the esteemed artists who contributed to a tribute album dedicated to Fats Domino, designed to assist in rebuilding Domino's home which was destroyed during Hurricane Katrina. "everyone from Elton John to Dr. John, from Paul McCartney to Robert Plant, will come together to record a tribute album to help raise funds to rebuild it."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Friendliness Towards The Trews
podcast.body: During their tour together, Robert Plant demonstrated remarkable friendliness towards The Trews. He introduced himself and checked out their guitars at their first soundcheck, leaving a lasting positive impression on the band. "He was so friendly. I mean, he came to our first sound check to like check out our guitars and introduce himself and just be a kind dude."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Joining Lésepirín
podcast.body: Robert Plan was discovered by Jimmy Page and John Paul Jones after they left The Jarpers and were seeking new members to form a band. His arrival completed the lineup that would become the legendary Lésepirín. "Empezarían a buscar a gente hasta que darían con Robert Plan y acabarían fondando el Ezepelín."

He was promoting his "Mighty ReArranger" album, often referred to as "strange sensation." "that was a whole tour. We did, we went from like Toronto to Victoria doing like the rinks."

xref.title: Touring with Robert Plant (2005)
xref.body: The Trews embarked on a full North American tour, "a dozen dates" from Toronto to Victoria, opening for Robert Plant, who was promoting his "Mighty ReArranger" album. Plant was noted for his friendliness, checking out their guitars at their first soundcheck and performing Led Zeppelin songs like "Going to California" and "That's The Way." "we were getting on a bus to tour with the Golden God himself."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Trews: In Their Own Words

xref.title: One-Night-Only Reunion (2007)
xref.body: Led Zeppelin reunited for a single, historic concert at the O2 in London on December 10, 2007. This event was prompted by the death of Ahmet Ertegun, the founder of Atlantic Records, who had signed the band in the late 1960s and was crucial to their rise. The lineup included Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, and John Paul Jones, with John's son, Jason Bonham, filling in on drums for his late father. It was the first significant appearance for Led Zeppelin in 27 years, attracting an overwhelming 20 million ticket applications. The band performed a 16-song set that night, but despite the massive success and acclaim, they have not played together again since. "On December 10th, 2007, Led Zeppelin reunited for a one night only concert at the O2 in London."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Filling in for Father
xref.body: Jason Bonham is the son of Led Zeppelin drummer John Bonham. He has been a member of several bands of his own and has notably sat in for his father on drums a couple of times when Jimmy Page and Robert Plant required a timekeeper. "He's not only been in a bunch of bands of his own, but he sat in for his dad on drums a couple of times when Jimmy Page and Robert Plant needed somebody to keep time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: The "Bohemian Rhapsody" Incident
xref.body: During their tour with Robert Plant, a fan dared The Trews on live radio to perform their old cover of Queen's "Bohemian Rhapsody" at a sold-out show in Rexall Place, Edmonton. The band delivered a "punky version" that garnered a standing ovation. This angered Robert Plant, who, having known Freddie Mercury, didn't want the past relived. He "accosted" their drummer, Sean, the next day in Calgary, but later issued a public apology by praising Canadian songwriters, including The Trews, at the Saddledome. "we got word that we really ticked Robert Plant off."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Trews: In Their Own Words

xref.title: Vocal Style Development
xref.body: Formed in 2012, Josh Kiszka, the singer, initially lacked his own vocal amplifiers. This forced him to develop a powerful vocal style to be heard over the guitars and drums, which, according to Jake Kiszka, naturally evolved into his Robert Plant-like delivery, likely also influenced by their exposure to old Led Zeppelin records. "Josh, for example, didn't have his own vocal amps, so he had to develop a style where he could be heard over the guitars and drums. And according to Jake, which is what he told me, this is how John ended up with that Robert Plant-like delivery."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
